title: Define upgrade/downgrade policy for AWS/GCP Marketplace buyers + internal plan transition behavior
creator: Nikhil Sharma
description:
Problem
Marketplace buyers routinely ask (1) how to upgrade/downgrade between Hosted/Dedicated/Private and (2) what happens in Redwood when they change/cancel a marketplace subscription. Today we treat marketplace entitlements as a single "plan" with incomplete rules, which causes:
- Confusing guidance from Sales/SE/CS (when to instruct buyers to buy a new SKU vs amend an existing one)
- Accidental service disruption on cancellation/downgrade
- Billing mismatches when customers have overlapping entitlements (e.g., base SKU + add-on, or new SKU purchased before old SKU is canceled)

Goal
Define a clear, enforceable upgrade/downgrade policy for AWS + GCP marketplace SKUs and specify how Redwood internal plan transitions behave when marketplace entitlements change.

Non-goals
- Re-platform internal billing or add bespoke proration/refunds beyond what marketplaces support
- Change SKU taxonomy itself (owned by PM-873); this ticket consumes the finalized taxonomy

Assumptions / constraints (validate with Partnerships/Finance)
- AWS/GCP marketplace generally treats many changes as "new subscription" or "change plan" with provider-specific constraints; buyers often cannot rely on mid-cycle proration.
- Redwood must be resilient to overlapping active entitlements during transitions (customers frequently buy the new SKU before canceling the old one to avoid downtime).

Proposed Policy (v1)

A) Definitions
- Base SKU = one of Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (mutually exclusive from a product packaging perspective)
- Add-on SKU = Compliance Pack, Observability Retention, Premium SLA (may be additive)
- Entitlement = the atomic permission granted to a Redwood org by marketplace webhook ingestion (ENG-4401)
- Effective plan in Redwood = the computed set of features/limits used by billing + enforcement

B) Allowed marketplace changes (what we support in-product)
1) Add-ons
- Add add-on: Supported, effective as soon as entitlement is ingested and linked to org.
- Remove add-on: Supported, but removal only takes effect at the end of the current marketplace billing period/term (depending on marketplace mechanics). Redwood will:
  - Continue honoring the add-on while the entitlement remains active.
  - Automatically remove add-on benefits once entitlement is no longer active.
- Rationale: Avoid surprises and align with common marketplace subscription semantics.

2) Base SKU upgrades
- Hosted -> Dedicated: Supported as "buy new base SKU". Customer purchases Dedicated SKU in marketplace; Redwood links new entitlement to the same org. Redwood switches effective base plan to Dedicated with no downtime.
- Dedicated -> Private: Supported as "buy new base SKU". Same as above.
- Hosted -> Private: Supported as "buy new base SKU".
- Note: We should not recommend "cancel old first". Guidance should be "buy new, validate, then cancel old".

3) Base SKU downgrades
- Private -> Dedicated / Hosted: Not supported as an in-console downgrade action. Customer must:
  - Purchase the lower-tier SKU (if they truly want to change), validate, then cancel the higher-tier SKU.
  - For Private, route through Sales/Partnerships for managed transition due to term/commit and required environment changes (VPC/on-prem).
- Dedicated -> Hosted: Same policy (purchase new Hosted SKU, validate, cancel Dedicated) and route through Sales for capacity/commit considerations.
- Rationale: Dedicated/Private are usually capacity/licensed with operational commitments; enforce predictable behavior and avoid accidental loss of SLA/capacity.

4) Lateral moves within same base family
- Hosted usage SKUs: allow switching between hosted usage tiers (if we expose multiple) only if marketplace natively supports plan changes without breaking subscription identity; otherwise treat as "buy new + cancel old".
- Dedicated sizes: treat as "managed change" (Sales-assisted) unless marketplace provides an explicit "dimension/quantity" update we can safely map.

C) Redwood internal plan computation rules (critical)
1) Precedence when multiple base entitlements are simultaneously active (overlap during transitions)
- Redwood will compute effective base plan as the highest-precedence active base entitlement:
  Private > Dedicated > Hosted
- If multiple active base entitlements exist at same precedence level (e.g., two Dedicated SKUs), Redwood selects the most recently activated entitlement (by entitlement start timestamp) and flags the org for review in internal tooling.

2) Add-on behavior with multiple entitlements
- Add-ons are unioned: if any active add-on entitlement exists, its features are enabled.
- If multiple add-ons conflict (e.g., two retention durations), Redwood selects the highest retention/most permissive SLA, but logs a warning for Billing review.

3) Cancellation/expiration behavior
- On base entitlement cancellation/expiration, Redwood falls back automatically to the next-highest active base entitlement (if present).
- Introduce a short "grace" window to protect against webhook delays:
  - If an entitlement is marked inactive, keep last-known effective plan for up to 60 minutes while we attempt re-fetch/retry ingestion (ENG-4401 retry semantics). After grace window, enforce the newly computed effective plan.
- If no base entitlements remain, org transitions to "Marketplace inactive" state:
  - API calls rejected with a clear error message including remediation instructions (re-purchase/link org, contact support).

4) Internal plan transition logging + audit
- All plan computations must be auditable (event log records: previous effective plan, new effective plan, reason, entitlement IDs, marketplace source).
- This is important for support (SUP tickets) and for finance reconciliation.

D) Customer-facing guidance (Docs + In-console copy)
- We will publish explicit upgrade/downgrade FAQs (ENG-4404/ENG-4405 docs scope) with consistent guidance:
  - "To upgrade: purchase the new plan first, then cancel the old plan after verification."
  - "Downgrades for Dedicated/Private are Sales-assisted; contact us."
  - "If you have multiple subscriptions temporarily, Redwood will use the highest-tier plan automatically."
- In-console: Marketplace onboarding wizard should include a section "Changing plans" with the same recommended sequence.

E) Sales/SE enablement rules of thumb (internal)
- If buyer asks for Dedicated/Private downgrade or mid-term change: steer to direct amendment (or direct contract) unless their procurement requires marketplace.
- If buyer wants to move spend to marketplace (existing direct customer): treat as a parallel entitlement period with controlled cutover date; do not promise proration/refunds without Finance approval.

Open questions
1) Do we ever allow Hosted downgrade to a cheaper Hosted tier self-serve (if marketplaces support)? If yes, we need explicit mapping to internal plan codes and meter descriptions.
2) How do we represent credits/discounts in marketplace terms (Finance/Legal)? This affects whether we tell customers "cancel and re-buy" vs "amend".
3) For Dedicated SKUs: can we safely map quantity changes (e.g., # of GPUs / capacity units) to entitlement quantities, or do we require a new SKU per size?

Acceptance criteria
- Written policy (this ticket) approved by PM (Lauren), Partnerships owner, Finance (Laura Bennett), and Solutions Engineering lead (Markus Klein) for field-facing guidance.
- Engineering requirements captured for:
  - Base precedence + add-on union rules (ENG-4406/ENG-4401)
  - Grace window + fallbacks + audit logs (ENG-4401/ENG-4402)
  - Console messaging (ENG-4403)
  - Docs updates (ENG-4404/ENG-4405)
- Support macros updated to reflect policy (ENG-4409).

Notes
- This policy is intentionally conservative for Dedicated/Private downgrades to prevent accidental SLA/capacity loss and reduce support escalations.
- Once we have stable telemetry on entitlement change flows post-launch, we can revisit more self-serve transitions (v2).
comments: 2025-02-10 — Markus Klein (Solutions Engineering): Please make the recommended sequence explicit: "buy new -> link org -> validate -> cancel old". We’ve seen prospects cancel first and then get blocked waiting on entitlement. Also add a line about overlap being okay and we’ll pick the highest tier.

2025-02-11 — Cole Summers (Billing): The precedence rule needs to be deterministic and recorded. Billing requires an event stream so we can reconcile invoice descriptors vs effective plan at any timestamp. Grace window is good; suggest 60 minutes max to avoid extended free access after cancellation.

2025-02-12 — Laura Bennett (Finance): +1 conservative downgrade posture. Please avoid language that implies proration/refunds. For marketplace renewals/cancellations, direct customers to marketplace terms and Redwood support for activation issues only.

2025-02-14 — Ethan Park (Eng, control plane): Engineering can implement "effective plan computation" as: selectBaseEntitlement() + mergeAddOns(); will need final SKU taxonomy + entitlement IDs from PM-873/ADR. Also note that some marketplace events come out-of-order; grace window should be paired with idempotent reprocessing.

2025-02-18 — Soojin Lee (PMM): For listings and FAQ, we should avoid saying "downgrade not allowed"; instead: "Dedicated/Private plan changes are Sales-assisted" and provide a contact path. Also, can we say "highest-tier plan will apply automatically" (confirm with Eng/Billing).

2025-02-21 — Lauren Bishop (PM): Proposed policy looks aligned. Remaining decision needed: whether Hosted tier-to-tier changes will be supported via marketplace 'change plan' (if AWS/GCP allow) or always 'buy new + cancel old'. Request Partnerships input before marking Done.
